content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in TypeScript: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.ts`. Build and run it with Deno — `deno run`, `deno check` and `deno test`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. ./main.ts ./BRIEF.md

content.text:
I added all four features to `main.ts`. It passes `deno check`, and I ran a sample command file that covered each one. The output matched the brief, and `add`, `done` and the line format of `list` behave as before. - **`prio

`** sets a task's priority and writes `prio

`. Tasks start at priority 5. An unknown id writes `no such task `. Anything other than a single digit 0–9 writes `bad priority

` and changes nothing; that covers `10`, `x` and a missing value. - **`list`** now shows open tasks sorted by priority, lowest first, with ties broken by id. - **`list all`** shows every task in the same order as ` `, with `-` for open and `x` for finished. - **Unknown commands** now write `? <word>`. Before, they were silently ignored. Where the brief was unclear, I made these choices: - If both the id and the priority are bad, the id is checked first, so you get `no such task <id>`. - Lines with only spaces count as blank and are still ignored. Without this they would now print `? `, which is new output on lines that used to print nothing. - `list` followed by anything other than `all` (for example `list foo`) still acts as plain `list`, as it did before. - The program still reads a file, so it needs read permission to run: `deno run --allow-read main.ts <file>`.
